The game's frame in a match, called from the end-of-frame interrupt (irq_frame_end) with interrupts on, and once at kick-off. Does nothing on the frame a scroll's drawing is half done. While paused ($07FE set) it only plays sound, reads the controls and unpauses on fire. Otherwise: sets the fine scroll from the scroll counters, finishes a scroll by a character (swap screens, draw the new row or column), sorts the sprites (mux_sort, or sprites_direct when 8 or fewer objects are on screen), moves the camera (camera_check and one to four scroll steps for its speed), then runs the players' control and the computer's play, the ball, the objects' movement and their collisions; on alternate frames reads the controls, or puts the objects on screen, flashes the controlled player and takes the pause key (P), the end key and the cheat keys. Every fourth frame it redraws the scores and the clock. Then it plays the sound, and once a second ($44 counts 50 frames) counts possession, runs the clock down a second and sounds the hooter at full time.
A false symbol: the BIT at $5D1F, $5D2C skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $20A9, which lies in match_frame.

With the cheat on ($0C10 set by typing BRADFORD-ON-AVON on the title screen), four keys act in a match: T calls $32AD for team 1, G calls $326C for the controlled player ($72), F calls $334E with $0E, and + adds the bonus $55 to team 1's score.

Once a second of play (every 50 frames, counted in $44): a second of possession for the holder's team ($0C01,x) and, in the opponents' half, a second there ($0C03,x); a new pickup (spawn_pickup), the running token's second (token_tick), and the clock down by one second in decimal; at 0 the half is over ($45 = 4) with effect $1E.
Ends a scroll by a character: clears the scroll flags ($8A, $8B), swaps the screen shown and the screen drawn into ($7C), and makes the new character position the camera's ($84 to $7E, $85 to $80).

The end of a half or the match: sets bit 6 of $45 (camera on a fixed point), takes control from both players ($72, $73 = $FF), clears the controls' state, stops the 18 players (targets $E472/$E48C), clears their moving and action flags, makes the ball the followed object and puts the ball back to the centre spot at column $27, row $4B.
A false symbol: the BIT at $612C skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $22A9, which lies in match_end_frame.
Turns the fine scroll counters ($81 across, $82 down, 0-7) into the camera's sub-character position ($7D, $7F) through fine_scroll_steps.
The camera's sub-character position for each fine scroll position, in 32nds: $E0 down to $00. Read by fine_scroll.

Moves the two controlled players for this frame by the game mode in $3B: 0 the computer plays both ($3E66 on $72 and $73); 1 one player on both joysticks against the computer (port 1 or port 2, either works); otherwise two players, team 1 on port 2 ($9C/$9E) and team 2 on port 1 ($9D/$9F), each through player_input ($3AA4), with a reversed joystick (bits 0 and 1 of $46, the token) swapped by reverse_stick first.
Reverses a joystick for the reverse-joystick token: swaps up with down and left with right in the held bits $3F and the new presses $40, keeping fire.

Marks which of the 26 objects are near enough to the camera to be drawn: sets bit 0 of $A0,x for those within 43 columns and 26 rows of the camera's corner (allowing 3 for the sprite's size), clears it for the others (and clears the off-screen players' action bits in $BA,x), and counts the visible ones in $59.

Moves the 18 players by their speeds ($E400/$E413 across, $E426/$E439 down, 8.8 fixed point), stopping each axis when it reaches the player's target ($E44C, $E45F) and bouncing it off the arena's walls (columns $08-$47, rows $08-$8E) by undoing the step and setting bit 6 (side) or bit 7 (end) of $A0,x. A goalkeeper ($1CC4 zero) in play keeps to his goal area, rows up to $1DB0 or from $1DD4 by the end his team defends ($1D8B). Then moves the ball the same way between columns $06-$49 and rows $06-$90.
Zeroes $0B33-$0BC2: the 144 bytes of league and cup results.
Zeroes the 32 bytes at $0BDB.

Resets the game for a new season: zeroes zero page from $02 to $FF and $07FE-$0C0C, sets every player attribute in $084E-$091F and $0AC3-$0B22 to 100, numbers the 12 squad places 0-11 ($0AB7), fills the 16-team table at $0B23 with each team's number in both nibbles, and starts the transfer market (transfer_init, $568E). Then runs on into match_reset.

Zeroes both scores and the two teams' injury counts ($6F, $70), keeps the two teams ($3C, $3D) in $0C0B/$0C0C, zeroes the 16 match statistics at $0BFB, marks all 18 players fit ($08DE = $FF; in practice, with no opponent ($3B negative), the other team's nine at $08E7 are cleared), puts the multiplier in the middle ($51 = 2, neither team) with what scoring is worth there (multiplier_points), and runs on into the clock's reset.
Sets the clock to 90 seconds ($4D = $90, BCD) and zeroes the ten counters at $0AA2.

Sets the teams' colours and the ends they play: the colours from $1D34 and $1D38 by $3D, the nine team-2 colours at $1D49 and $1D54; when the side in $3E differs from the formation tables' ($1D8B), swaps each of the seven pairs of formation tables (the two teams' columns and rows in attack and defence, and the goalkeepers' limits) and sets each player's end. Then each player's resting column, halfway between his attack and defence columns, into $E576.

The list unpack_list ($4B55) takes at match_setup's $26E2: a count (4), then four entries of packed source and destination: $9C1C to $BCEF (the pitch's block map), $A751 to $F800 (the arena's characters), $AB9B to $F000 (the panel's screen) and $AD33 to $F370.

Sets up a match. Unpacks the match sprites from $A04F to $E000 and turns their $40 frames ($80-$BF) from columns to rows (sprite_rows), $30 more from $A1D0 to $C000 (frames $00-$2F), and ten from $A5BB (door_sprites) over the first ten of those, for the run-out; with all RAM in, copies 23 frames (sprite_copy, list copy_pairs) and makes 45 left-facing frames as mirror images of right-facing ones (sprite_mirror, list mirror_pairs); unpacks the pitch's block map, the arena's characters and the panel (arena_unpack_list), and makes mirror images of 52 arena characters ($F800 to $F9A0), 47 more ($FC00 to $FD78) and 15 of the panel's ($F110 to $F098) through the pixel-pair table sprite_mirror left at $0920 (map_translate): the arena's right side is its left side mirrored. Then the teams' sides, the players' state (speeds, targets, sprite frames $40, colours, positions from the formation tables), the ball at the centre, the camera on the ball, the colours ($5A-$5F), clears colour RAM, draws the pitch and the panel, sets up the multiplexer, runs the first frame and the players' run-out: they walk to their places, the ball is launched with effects $1C and $1D, and then the frames from $A1D0 are unpacked again over the door ($29B6) and five more mirrored, the rest of the coin's spin ($1E-$22). The clock starts at 50 frames to the first second.
A false symbol: the BIT at $452B skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $27A9, which lies in match_setup.
A false symbol: the BIT at $16E9 skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $28A9, which lies in match_setup.
Copies A blocks of 8 bytes from ($1A) to ($1C), each byte through the 256-byte table at $0920.

Pairs of sprite frames for sprite_mirror: a frame and the frame to hold its mirror image, a left-facing figure from a right-facing one; 45 pairs used by match_setup ($26D4), then from $2A65 five more, the coin's spin $1E-$22, after the run-out unpacks arena_sprites again ($29DC). A frame number N is the 64 bytes at $C000 + 64N.
23 pairs of sprite frames for sprite_copy ($26CB): a frame and the frame it is copied to, for figures used unchanged in another place in the set.

Places the two arcs over the controlled players ($72 team 1, $73 team 2) as objects 19 and 20: copies each player's position (three rows higher) and colour to the marker, and its frame from $1CB2 when that player has the ball (0, no frame, otherwise); a marker whose player is not controlled or not on the pitch is moved off ($E0, $DF = $FA).

Once a frame, in a match. Gives each human team the player who has the ball, or the nearest one to it (nearest_player), as its controlled player, stopping his own run; then, when the ball is free ($60 = $12), moves it: its height ($63) rises and falls by the vertical speed $64, which drops by one a frame (gravity), and its frame shows the height. A bounce off an end wall turns its vertical speed round and, between columns $22 and $2D below height $40, is a goal for the team attacking that end, unless the goal-door token protects it: counts the goal ($0BFD), adds the goal's points ($53,x, with the multiplier) to the score, lets the scorer celebrate (frame $A1, a run up the pitch), sets the goal state ($45 = 2) and plays effect $18; any other end-wall bounce plays effect $0C. Then the score multiplier ramps ($2C61), the bounce domes (bounce_dome), the electrobounce units (electrobounce), the ball slowing down every 7 frames and coming off the walls, losing the ball when it is more than two away from its holder, and picking it up (pick_up, $2D59).
A false symbol: the BIT at $2F0E skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $2BA9, which lies in ball_frame.

The ball runs up a score multiplier ramp (rows $48-$49 going down, $4B-$4C going up, at the sides of the pitch): moves the multiplier $51 a step towards the team whose player threw it (0 or 1 for team 1, 3 or 4 for team 2, 2 for neither), recomputes the goals' worth and the panel lights (multiplier_points, $34C7) and holds the ball in the ramp for two passes of 31 frames ($69, ramp_ride).
A false symbol: the BIT at $388F skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $2CA9, which lies in multiplier_ramp.

A free ball within one column and one row of a player who is not down and did not just lose it, and low enough (or the player jumping), is his: he becomes the ball's holder ($60) and takes the possession colour ($1D53 or $1D54), with effect $14. A goalkeeper who takes the ball from the other team counts a save ($0BFF). A ball the other team electrified (bit 6 or 7 of $46, by $1C9E) instead knocks the player down (tackle, $3868) and uses up one of its charges ($65); when they are gone it is an ordinary ball again.

Finds the player of a team nearest the player Y (the ball holder or the ball): A = 0 for team 1 or 9 for team 2, X the team's controlled player, measured first ($FF when he cannot be used). Then every fourth player of the team, from (frame counter $42 / 2) AND 3, so two or three players a call and a different set every second frame. The distance is the column plus row distance, 10 more for a player off screen; a goalkeeper counts only while Y's row lies inside the goalkeeper's area ($1DB0, $1DD4) and he is on screen; players with $A0,x = 0 are skipped. Returns the nearest in A.

The ball hits one of the two bounce domes on the centre line (rows $2A-$2E and $6A-$6E): sends it back off the dome (bounce_away), gives the team that threw it the dome's bonus ($55,x, score_add), shows the dome flashing (object 21, frame $BC, for 6 frames) and plays effect $22.
A false symbol: the BIT at $4528 skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $2EA9, which lies in bounce_dome.

The ball rolls through an electrobounce unit (left wall at rows $6B-$6F, right wall at rows $27-$2B): sends it back off the wall with effect $24, and, when a player threw it, electrifies it for his team (bit 7 of $46 for team 1, 6 for team 2) with that team's charges ($57 or $58 into $65), turns it yellow and frees it; the unit flashes (object 21, frame $BD or $BE).

Sets the ball's vertical speed for a bounce: A less than 2 sends it up the screen, more than 2 down, and 2 stops it; at speed $96, or the thrower's throw speed from $383F when the ball was thrown; returns the speed in $22. Clears the ball's slowing counters ($67, $68).

Once a second, puts a new pickup on the pitch in the first free slot of objects 22-25 that may take it: half the time a coin (type $14), otherwise a random type 0-31. Armour (0-7) goes only in slot 22 and only while nobody wears any ($6B negative); tokens (8-19) only in slots 23-25, the reverse joystick (9) only in a two-player game ($0AAC = 2); coins ($14 and over, coloured 6) only while neither team has more than the game type's most ($0AB5). It shows as frame type + 6 at a random column 8-$47 outside the centre ($24-$2B) and a random row $10-$8F, with effect 5.
A false symbol: the BIT at $476D skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $3069, which lies in spawn_pickup.
Animates one of the four pickups each frame (the frame counter picks which): a spinning coin steps through frames $1A-$25 and round again.
A player (X) touches pickup object Y: removes it ($A0,y = 0) and runs the handler for its type (frame - 6, 0-31) from pickup_handlers through $29: types 0-7 armour, 8-19 tokens, 20-31 coins.

The 32 pickup types' handlers. Types 0-7 are armour, each raising one attribute (armour_wear): type 0 SPD ($3115), 1 INT ($3129), 2 DEF ($3110), 3 ATT ($310B), 4 POW ($311F), 5 STA ($3124), 6 THR ($311A), 7 AGR ($3106). Types 8-19 are the tokens, in the order the coaching manual lists them: freeze team ($334E), reverse joystick ($32FB), reduce team ($330B), increase team ($331A), manic ($3329), slow team ($3339), grab ball ($326C), transport ($3288), goal door ($32DB), shield ($32EB), full energy ($32D1), zap team ($32AD). Types 20-31 are coins ($30F7).
The high bytes of pickup_handlers' addresses.
The offset of each of the eight attributes in the players' attribute table at $084E (18 players each): AGR $00, ATT $12, DEF $24, SPD $36, THR $48, POW $5A, STA $6C, INT $7E.
A coin: effect $0A, and one more coin for the player's team ($4F team 1, $50 team 2); the coins are paid into the bank after the match.

The armour pickups' common part: Y = the attribute (0-7) for each piece's entry at $3106-$312B. Raises that attribute of player X halfway to 255 (keeping the old value in $6D, and in the token copy at $EE00 while a token runs), marks him as wearing armour ($6B = X, $6C = the attribute) and plays effect $12.
The player wearing armour is tackled: puts his attribute back to the value before, and the first time the piece falls off (object 22 placed where he is, with the piece's frame).

Starts a token's 10-second run ($4E): keeps a copy of all attributes at $EE00 (unless one runs already), draws the token's symbol in the panel on the side of the team that took it (characters $50-$55 at $F376 or $F390, the sprite frame's picture copied into the panel's characters at $F283) and plays effect 6.
Once a second, while a token runs: counts it down with a tick (effect 7); at the end plays effect 3 and ends it (token_end).

Ends the running token: clears the token bits of $46 (keeping the electric ball's), restores every attribute from the copy at $EE00, unfreezes all players and puts the panel's characters back (token_panel_cells).
Where token_end puts back the panel's characters: twelve offsets from $F370, then ($3260) the characters to put there.
The characters token_end puts back, after token_panel_cells' twelve offsets.
Grab ball (token 14, and the G cheat key): player X takes the ball: the old holder gets his team's colour back, X becomes the holder ($60) in the possession colour, effect $28.
Transport (token 15): the ball goes to the team's player in place 6 of its formation ($1CF6,x + 6, the forward) with effect $26.
Zap team (token 19, and the T cheat key): every player of the other team on the pitch is tackled down (tackle), with effect $0E. Not during a stoppage ($45 set).
Full energy (token 18): the player's energy back to 255 and effect $27.
Goal door (token 16): sets bit 2 (team 1) or 3 (team 2) of $46: the goal is shut to the other team's shots.
Shield (token 17): bit 4 or 5 of $46: the team's players cannot be tackled.
Reverse joystick (token 9): bit 1 or 0 of $46 reverses the other team's joystick (reverse_stick).
Reduce team (token 10): every attribute of the other team's nine players to 0 (team_attributes) for the token's time.
Increase team (token 11): every attribute of the team's nine players to 255 for the token's time.
Manic (token 12): every attribute of all 18 players to 255 for the token's time.
Slow team (token 13): the other team's speed (attribute 3, $0884) to 0 for the token's time.
Freeze team (token 8, and the F cheat key): sets bit 2 of $A0 for the other team's players on the pitch, which stops objects_move moving them, for the token's time.

Colours the pitch's two halves: multicolour 2 above and below the centre line ($5C, $5D) from the team colours at $1D48, lit for the team the multiplier favours ($51), with the colour change (raster command $88) put at the centre line's raster line in $08 when the line is on screen and the two colours differ.

The ball bounces off a side wall: at a star's row (four rows a star, five stars on each side) lights the star for the attacking team and gives it the bonus ($55,x) through star_light, or, thrown by the defending team, puts a lit star out and takes the bonus back (star_unlight, score_sub). At the warp gates, two on each wall (rows $2F-$32 and $63-$66), it moves the ball to the other side wall (column 9 from the right wall, $46 from the left) and sends it on away from that wall at its thrower's throw speed, with effect $23. Otherwise it turns the ball's sideways speed round and frees it, with effect $0C unless a star changed.
A warp gate on the right wall: the ball comes out of the left wall's gate at column 9, moving right.
A warp gate on the left wall: the ball comes out of the right wall's gate at column $46, moving left.
The thrower's ($61) throw speed (throw_speed).

Sets what scoring is worth for the multiplier position $51 (0-4, 2 is neither team): a goal, an injury or a row of five stars ($53 team 1, $54 team 2: 20, 15, 10, 10, 10 and the reverse, in BCD), a star or a dome ($55, $56: 4, 3, 2, 2, 2), and the electric ball's charges, the opponents it tackles ($57, $58: 3, 2, 1, 1, 1).

Lights star Y (0-4 team 1's side, 5-9 team 2's) if it is out: marks it in $0AA2,y, starts the five-star check timer ($52 = 12), plays effect $19 and draws its lit block (star_draw). Returns with carry set if it lit, clear if it was lit already.

Draws the block for star or light Y (0-13) on the pitch: A = the block number (from star_lit_blocks, or the caller's); writes it into the block map at the star's place (star_map_lo/hi) and, when on screen, its 4 by 4 characters into the hidden screen (star_screen_lo/hi, $28 more for the screen at $CC00), clipped to 40 columns and 22 rows. Sets $8B to 3 so the next frame redraws.
Puts star Y out if it is lit (star_out_blocks); returns with carry set if it did.
When the five-star timer runs out: if all five stars on a side are lit, puts them all out and gives the side's team a goal's worth ($53,x) more, with effect $1A.
Returns non-zero when the five stars from Y are all lit.
Draws the four lights of the score multiplier for its position $51 (blocks from multiplier_light_blocks, map places 10-13) and colours the pitch's halves (pitch_halves_colour).
Draws every lit star again (after the pitch is drawn afresh).

The ball rides the score multiplier ramp: its place along the ramp's curve, from ramp_path_x and ramp_path_y, mirrored for the side ($6A bit 1) and the direction ($6A bit 0). The ride is two passes of 31 frames ($69): at the end of the first ($6A EOR $81) it lights the multiplier (multiplier_lights) with effect $25, unless the multiplier was at its end already ($6A bit 6), and rides back; at the end of the second it sends the ball out down or up the pitch.
The ramp's curve across: 32 steps, each a column (high nibble) and a sixteenth (low nibble), read by ramp_ride.
The ramp's curve down: 32 steps, the row offset from $48 and a sixteenth, read by ramp_ride.
The pitch row of each of the 14 places star_draw writes (ten stars, four multiplier lights).
Their pitch column.
Their address in the block map, low byte ($3771) and high byte ($377F).
The high bytes of star_map_lo's addresses.
Their address on the screen at $F400, low byte ($378D) and high byte ($379B), less the camera's offset.
The high bytes of star_screen_lo's addresses.
The block number of a lit star, team 1's five ($4F) and team 2's ($50, $51).
The block number of a star that is out.
The blocks of the four multiplier lights for each of the five positions ($37BD, $37C2, $37C7, $37CC): lit ($52-$55) or out.
The multiplier lights' blocks for position 1.
For position 2.
For position 3.
A byte ($EA) after the multiplier lights' table that nothing reads.

Player X throws the ball in direction A: the ball becomes free with X as its thrower ($61, $62), held low, his colour back, he plays the throw frame ($70 + 3 x direction) for 3 frames, the ball starts at his place and its speed for the direction comes from throw_dirs at the throw speed (throw_speed), with effect 1.
A player's throw speed: his THR attribute ($0896,x) / 4 + $74, at most $A5.
Player X jumps or slides: sets his action bit 3 for 4 frames and the jump frame for his direction ($88-$8F), effect 4.

Player X tackles player Y: Y falls (down for 12 + (255 - X's energy) / 32 frames, frame $98, effect $2C or $2E by team) and is knocked away from X at X's speed / 4; a ball holder loses the ball to X (or it stays free when X is the electric ball), and one wearing armour loses it. The damage is X's power / 2 + $4B less Y's stamina / 2, over 16: half of it (at least 1) comes off each of Y's eight attributes, to no less than 90, and all of it (at least 1) off his energy. Below zero he is injured (injured), and the other team scores a goal's worth ($53,x, through score_add_bcd, so it is not counted as a bonus).
The injury scores for the other team: what a goal is worth to it now ($53,x).

Player Y is injured and stretchered off: energy refilled, stopped, sent to his resting place, frame $9F, effect 9; the match stops ($45 = 1). The team's injury count goes up and the player changes places with the next substitute in the squad (his attributes swapped with the substitute's at $08F0, through injury_subs). tackle, the caller, then gives the other team a goal's worth.
Which substitute's attributes come on for each injury (by team and count): offsets into $08F0 of eight bytes a substitute.
Goalkeeper X dives left: the dive frame for his end ($B0 + 4 x end), a sideways speed of -$70 (moving left), action bit 5 (diving) and its timer cleared.
Goalkeeper X dives right: frame $B2 + 4 x end, sideways speed $70, action bit 5.
Player X slides along the ground: action bit 2 for 4 frames, the slide frame for his direction ($48-$4F), effect $1B.

A controlled player X (not down, sliding, diving or injured) answers the joystick in $3F (held) and $40 (new presses). Steers the ball while it flies (aftertouch, ball_steer at $4907); runs in the stick's direction (run_dir through stick_dirs, less the directions blocked in $E500,x); on a new fire press: with the ball, throws it the way he faces; a goalkeeper without it dives left or right with the stick; with the ball held by another player, tackles (action bit 0 while fire is held); with the ball free, jumps for a high ball or slides for a low one when moving.

Runs a quarter of the players each frame (the frame counter picks which). For each one on screen and not busy: an opponent within two cells is tackled when this player is tackling (bits 0 or 2) or is a computer player whose aggression ($084E) beats his threshold ($E524), the opponent is not shielded (bit 4 or 5 of $46 by $1C8C), and a random number is above 128 + the opponent's DEF / 2 - this player's ATT / 2; the tackle counts in the team's statistics ($0C05). Otherwise the two block each other's way ($E500,x). Then any pickup within two cells is taken (pickup_take). Then the player's action timer: at its end a throw lets the ball go (throw_aftertouch), a celebration ends the goal ($45 = 5), a jump lands (effect $16) and a stretcher leaves the pitch ($45 = 7). Then his frame for running, standing or the goalkeeper's stance, and a computer player's coroutine (player_resume).
Clears from player X's free directions ($E500,x) the bits not in A: the ways another player blocks (players_contact).

Animates the players while play is stopped ($45 three or more): half of them each frame, the run frames ($50 + 4 x direction + step) or the standing frame ($40 + direction), and runs each one's coroutine.

When the thrower's throw ends and a human threw it, the stick still held adds to the ball: fire lobs it (vertical speed $10, height $4A), and a direction adds a quarter of the throw speed across or down where the ball is not already moving that way, halving its slowing counters.
Resumes computer player X's coroutine: pushes the address kept at $E48C,x (high) and $E472,x (low), less one, and returns into it. A coroutine gives the frame back with player_yield.

Ends a computer player's turn: takes the caller's return address off the stack into $E472/$E48C for the player in $41, so that the next player_resume carries on after the call, and returns to player_resume's caller.
The idle coroutine every player starts with: yields, and yields again.

The computer's control of a team's controlled player X when the computer plays that team (in place of player_input): thinks every 2, 4 or 6 frames by his intelligence ($08CC: $C8 and over, $96 and over, less). Without the ball: jumps for a high free ball within two cells; a goalkeeper keeps goal (keeper_ai); others run for a pickup within four cells (pickup_near), or for the ball or its holder, or, while the ball rides a ramp, for the other team's controlled player. With the ball: a goalkeeper passes (pass_ball); others throw when placed for a shot (shot_check); dodge an opponent nearer than dodge_distance; at times (a random number against his intelligence, half for a forward) go for a pickup; otherwise run towards the goal, halfway to the end of their formation area each time, trying the two diagonals when the way is the opponent's, and when every way leads into him, a forward (role 3) shoots (shoot) and the others pass (pass_ball).
A false symbol: the BIT at $5A66 skips the two-byte instruction inside it; no instruction names $3EA9, which lies in player_ai.

Steps player X towards the column $75 and row $77: picks the joystick bits for the way (8 right, 4 left, 2 down, 1 up), drops those blocked ($E500,x), turns them into a direction (stick_dirs) and runs (run_dir); when every way is blocked he tackles (action bit 0).
Carry clear and Y the pickup when one of the four pickups (objects 22-25) on screen is within four columns and four rows of player X; carry set when none is.

Carry set and A a direction (0 up, 1 up-right, 2 right ... 7 up-left) when computer player X with the ball is placed to throw at something worth points: at a side wall by the multiplier ramp's mouth (rows $3B-$58, column below $0A or $46 and over), when the multiplier is not yet all his team's (f_40D1) and no opponent is within dodge_distance, into the ramp (down above row $4A, up below it); beside the left or right wall at a star's row whose star is not his team's, at the star (left or right); and, when the ball is not electric, on the diagonal that leads into an electrobounce unit (down-left towards the left one, up-right towards the right). Carry clear otherwise.
The multiplier position each team is aiming for (0 for team 1, 4 for team 2), by the team number at $1D08; shot_check does not aim at the ramp once it is there.
The joystick bits from player X towards the row $77, keeping his column (held between 9 and $47), through stick_towards.
Sets $75 halfway from player X's column to his formation's left limit ($1D9E) and returns the diagonal joystick bits up-left (5) or down-left (6) by the end he attacks.
The same towards the right limit ($1DC2): up-right (9) or down-right ($0A).

Computer player X passes. With the other team's controlled player within dodge_distance, an outfield player dodges him; a goalkeeper lobs the ball left or right (stick 4 or 8), to the side away from him, through throw_lob. Otherwise looks through his team for the nearest player of the next line up (player_lines, $1CD7, + 1) who is not down, avoiding one in the same direction as the opponent unless nearer than him; throws at where that player will be (lead_target, stick_towards), lobbing the ball (height $14, rising $13) when the receiver is further than his THR / 4. With no one to pass to he throws the ball upfield, away from the opponent (throw_away).
The pass's search loop goes on here for each candidate (pass_ball).
Throws the ball in direction A (throw) and lobs it: height $14, vertical speed $13.

Computer player X shoots at the goal he attacks: straight up or down the pitch when he is between the goal posts' columns ($22-$2D), or diagonally towards the goal when he is as far from the posts across as he is from the goal line, otherwise straight across towards the posts.
Throws the ball up the pitch (team 1's end 0) or down it, and to the right or left away from the opponent ($25 bit 1), lobbed (throw_lob).

The computer's goalkeeper X when he is on screen: slides at a holder of the ball within four cells; dives at a free ball within six cells that will pass him, left or right by its side (keeper_dive_left, keeper_dive_right); otherwise, when the ball is moving, or his aggression ($084E) / 2 is at least his threshold ($E524), moves to where the ball will be (lead_target), kept to his area (go_in_area); else stands in front of the goal (keeper_place).
The distance from player X to object Y, columns plus rows.
The joystick bits from player X towards object Y (its column and row into $75 and $77, then stick_towards).

The joystick bits (8 right, 4 left, 2 down, 1 up) from player X towards the column $75 and row $77, dropping the across part when it is less than a quarter of the distance down, and the down part when it is less than a quarter of the distance across.

The coroutine that walks player X to his kick-off place ($1D55 column, $1D67 row) at speed $60 a frame on each axis, facing the way he walks, or along the pitch (the end he plays, $1D8B) once there. match_setup gives it to every player for the run-out.

The coroutine of every player the joystick does not control, run on his turn (player_resume). Y is his team's controlled player (player 6, the forward, or 15 for a team the computer plays). Within 6 cells of Y he steps aside (step_aside). Every 2, 3 or 4 turns by his intelligence he picks a new place to go, and a new random threshold ($E524): a goalkeeper the goal mouth (keeper_place); with Y down, where the ball's holder will be (lead_target); a forward (role 3 and over, $1CC4) a place from forward_places when Y is near the end (forward_place); a defender (role 1) covers Y, or the player at $1CF6 when Y is a defender too (cover); a midfielder (role 2) covers Y when Y is within his columns ($1D9E-$1DC2) and otherwise holds his row (hold_row). In between he keeps running at the place ($E44C, $E45F, go_on).
Makes the column $75 and row $77 player X's target ($E44C, $E45F) and runs at it (go_on).
Runs player X towards his target ($E44C, $E45F), less the blocked directions, or stops him (all four speeds zero) when he is there or every way is blocked.
A place eight columns and six rows from object Y, on player X's side of it, into $75 and $77.

The goalkeeper's place: across, where the ball is heading (lead_target), held within the goal mouth ($21-$2E) and moved along the line between the ball and the goal line ($8E row for one end, $08 for the other by $1D8B) when the ball is outside it; down, on his goal line.

A forward's place when Y is within $1A rows of the end (from row 0, or from $95 for a team playing the other way, $1D8B): from forward_places, the row by that distance / 4 (six rows on for role 4) and the pair by Y's column / 4 (mirrored for the right half), held within his formation's area; further away he covers Y (cover).

Player X's place to support Y: across, halfway between Y's column and his resting column ($E576), within his formation's columns; down, Y's row moved by the distance across, towards one end or the other by the end he plays and whether his role ($1CD7) is below Y's, unless Y is beyond his resting row ($E588) that way, then halfway to Y (hold_row's end). Held within his area.

Player X's place level with Y across (within his columns) and, down, halfway between Y's row and his resting row ($E588), or between Y's row and his area's limit, by which side of the resting row Y is and which end he plays.
Holds the place $75, $77 within player X's formation area ($1D9E-$1DC2 across, $1DB0-$1DD4 down) and runs at it (go_to).

Where object Y will be: its position plus its speed times 1, 2, 4 or 8 by player X's intelligence ($08CC: below $64, $64 and over, $96, $C8), the column into $75 (fraction $74) and the row into $77 (fraction $76).

Runs player X in direction A (0-7): keeps it as his facing ($E4B9) and sets his two speeds through run_dir_routines, at his SPD / 4 plus $30, or plus $20 when he holds the ball: a player with the ball runs slower.

The eight routines run_dir calls, one a direction: up ($4783), up-right ($4798), right ($47AD), down-right ($47BC), down ($47CB), down-left ($47DA), left ($47EF), up-left ($4804). Each sets the speeds across ($E400/$E413) and down ($E426/$E439) from the speed in A: the same speed on both axes for a diagonal.
The high bytes of run_dir_routines' addresses.
Direction 0, up: speed down -A, across 0.
Direction 1: across +A, down -A.
Direction 2: across +A, down 0.
Direction 3: across +A, down +A.
Direction 4: down +A, across 0.
Direction 5: down +A, across -A.
Direction 6: across -A, down 0.
Direction 7: across -A, down -A.

The low bytes of twelve rows of forward_places (high byte at $4823, all $48): forward_place picks a row by the ball's distance from the goal / 4, for a distance below $1A, so 0-6, plus 6 for role 4. Role 3's index 6 is role 4's first row, and role 4's index 12 reads past the twelve, taking $48 from $4823 as the low byte and $1A from $482F as the high.
The high bytes of forward_places' row addresses (all $48), and then forward_places from $482F.
The forwards' places, eighteen pairs of column and row in each of the twelve rows, by the ball's column / 2.
Takes A off player X's speed across and Y off his speed down, each towards zero and no further (slow_across, slow_down_y / slow_up_y).
Adds Y's amount ($23) to a negative speed down ($E426/$E439), stopping at zero.
Takes $23 off a positive speed down, stopping at zero.

The game's unpacker: from ($2E) to ($30). A byte below $80 is a run of literals, that many plus one, copied as they are; a byte of $80 or more copies earlier output, from 256 - that byte back, for the length in the next byte; a length of 0 ends the data.
A pseudo-random number in $2D (and A): the last one plus $35, the raster line ($D012) and SID voice 3's oscillator ($D41B).
Starts SID voice 3 as a noise generator at its highest frequency, muted ($D418 = $8F: voice 3 off), for random's oscillator reads.
Stops voice 3's noise and sets full volume.
Waits for the raster to pass line 256 ($D011 bit 7 falling then rising): once a frame.
Fills from ($1A) up to ($1C) with A.
Copies from ($1E) to ($1A) up to ($1C).

Reads the controls. Joystick port 2 into $9C and port 1 into $9D (bits set while held: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire), the new presses since the last read into $9E and $9F. When a key is held and joystick 1 is still, scans the keyboard: each row's held keys into $94-$9B and the new presses into $8C-$93 (row r is $94 + r, column c is bit c, so key 8 x r + c), and the keys in key_sticks stand in for the sticks: I, M, J, K and SPACE for port 2, A, Z, comma, full stop and / for port 1, RUN/STOP for both (bit 5). Otherwise clears the key state.
Unpacks every entry of the list at (X low, Y high): a count, then four bytes an entry, the packed data's address and its destination (unpack).
An interrupt handler that only acknowledges the CIA.
The RESTORE key's interrupt: goes to the main menu ($6E8E) without returning.
Jumps through the address in $29 and $2A (the callers' JSR makes it an indirect call).
A = (X x 256 + A) / Y, eight bits of quotient, the remainder in $22.
A = A x X, the low eight bits.
A x 10.
A x 10 + 100: a team rating digit (0-15) as an attribute.
Waits for the next frame, reads the controls and runs on into tape_motor.

Keeps the cassette motor bit of the processor port ($01 bit 5) as it was, from $0C0E, unless a key on the cassette (sense bit 4) is up, when it turns the motor off; the other port bits are I/O in, BASIC and KERNAL out ($15).

Fades the screen to black over 16 frames (8 for a bitmap screen): each frame turns every colour into the next darker one (darker_colour): the background and multicolours ($5A-$5F, $D021-$D023), the sprites' colours, the objects' colours ($0A3A) and colour RAM (fade_colour_ram, or fade_bitmap_colours through the paired table it builds at $0920).
Darkens colour RAM for a character screen: each colour through darker_mc, which keeps the multicolour bit.
Darkens a bitmap's colours: colour RAM and the screen at $CC00 (both nibbles) through the table at $0920.
Sixteen colours from dark to light (0, 11, 9, 2, 6, 14, 4, 10, 8, 12, 5, 7, 15, 3, 13, 1) that nothing reads.
Each colour's next darker colour, for fade_out: white to cyan, cyan to yellow, yellow to light grey and so on down to black.
The same for multicolour character colours (8-15 stay multicolour).

Turns A sprite frames at (X, Y) from columns (21 bytes for each of the three columns) into the VIC's rows (three bytes a row); then, when $26 is not zero, makes $26 mirror images from (X, Y) on to ($1C) (sprite_mirror).
Fills $0920 with each byte's mirror image in pixel pairs (multicolour pixels): the four pairs in the other order.
Mirrors the sprite frame at ($1A) into ($1C): each row's three bytes swapped end for end and each through mirror_table.
Makes A mirror images, from the list of frame pairs at (X, Y) (frame_pair_addr): the second frame of each pair becomes the first's mirror image.
Copies A frames from the list of pairs at (X, Y): the first to the second, or the second to the first when carry was set.
Reads the next pair of frame numbers at ($1E) and turns them into addresses at $C000 + 64 x frame, ($1A) and ($1C).
Builds a menu screen from the list at $8527: unpacks the tiles to $C000, each cell's flip bits to $007A and the map of tiles to $C800, then draws it (tile_screen).
The same from the list at $7D72, with the map at $CC00; then colours the last three rows ($CF70-$CFE7) white on black ($10).
Shows the bitmap picture at $7AFC (show_picture).

Draws a menu screen whose list is at (X, Y) and map is at A x 256: unpacks it, and with carry set first fills the map's $FF cells from the screen at $F400 (tile_fill). Then draws every cell's tile into the bitmap at $E000 (draw_tile), each with two flip bits from $007A on (four cells a byte).
Where the map at $CC00 holds $FF, takes the cell from $F400.

Draws tile A (10 bytes each from ($20): eight bytes of pixels, a screen colour byte and a colour RAM byte) into the bitmap cell at ($1A), turned upside down when bit 1 of $24 is set and mirrored (mirror_table) when bit 0 is, and its two colour bytes into the screen at $CC00 and colour RAM.

Shows a bitmap picture from the list at (X, Y): black border; unless $36 is set, unpacks the list's third entry to $CC00 and copies it into colour RAM first; then unpacks the list (bitmap, screen and colours).

Waits for a frame, clears the VIC's sprite registers, turns on all eight multicolour sprites, sprite multicolour 2 light grey, and shows the multicolour bitmap at $E000 with its screen at $CC00 ($D018 = $38, $D011 = $3B, $D016 = $1B).
Moves the sprites to the menus' multiplexer (mux_menus), fades the screen out (fade_out) and blanks it, sprites off, $36 clear.

Prints mini-font character A into the bitmap at ($1A), in pixel pairs of colour bits 0 (Y = 0); entered at $507A it prints in colour $55. Two pixels a nibble, through the pairs table at $1C2A, the next cell every eight rows. Moves ($1A) on a cell.
print_char's entry for colour $55 (colour 1 in every pixel pair).
Prints the high nibble of A as a row of pixel pairs (print_char).
Prints the low nibble of A as a row of four pixels through nibble_pairs, keeping the other pixels, and moves to the next row.
Prints mini-font character A five rows tall at ($1C) in colour 1 (the bits $55 of the pairs table), and moves on a cell.
print_char_tall's row from a high nibble.
print_char_tall's row from a low nibble.
Sets the multicolour pixel at column $34, row $35 of the bitmap at $E000 to colour A (0-3).

Prints the text at ($1A), ending with 0, in the big font at $C000 (letters of 16 by 16 pixels, two cells across and two down: the top two cells' 16 bytes, and the bottom two's 128 bytes on, eight letters to a page): starting at column X of text row Y (big_text_rows: rows of the bitmap at $E000), each letter merged into what is there (merge_byte). A space leaves a gap.
Merges byte Y of the letter at ($1E) into the bitmap at ($1C): its pixels and those beside them cleared first, giving the letter an outline.
Prints the text at ($1C), letters $00-$3F, into sprite frames from ($1A) on (sprite_char): 1 starts the next line ten rows down; 0 ends.
Prints mini-font character A into the sprite data at ($1A), at text column X (two letters a byte across), row Y.
Moves on a row in sprite_char's sprite data.
The offset in the sprite data for row $23 and byte $22: three bytes a row, past a frame's 63 bytes into the next frame's.
Draws 32 sprite figures into the bitmap at $E000 pixel by pixel (plot): frame f_66DE,x (from $C000; $BF ends early) at column f_6696,x / 2 + $4E, row f_66BA,x, 12 by 21 pixels.

Gives team 2 the ratings of team A (1-16) through the packed routine after the JSR (run_packed, unpacked to $C000): each of its eight attributes from team_ratings' digits, 100 + 10 x digit (rating_to_attr), the same for players 9-11, 12-14 and 15-17 in turn, then the substitutes' at $0908, $0910 and $0918.
The packed routine team_2_ratings unpacks to $C000 and runs: $C000 the loop over three groups of three players, $C056 one digit to three players, $C068 one digit to three substitutes.
Swaps the two human teams' squads (the 96 bytes at $0AC3 and at $0B23), their four bytes at $0AB1-$0AB4 and the team numbers $3C and $3D.
Copies the squad at $0AC3 into team 2's players (squad_to_team from player 9, substitutes from $18).
Copies the squad at $0AC3 into the match's attribute table for team 1: for each of the eight attributes, nine players to $084E + 18 x attribute, then the three substitutes to $08F0, $08F8 and $0900.

Records the match between teams $3C and $3D in the league table, through the packed routine after the JSR (run_packed), in decimal: a win ($3A = 1 or 2) adds one to the winner's wins ($0B33) and the loser's defeats ($0B53) and 10 points to the winner ($0BA3/$0BB3); a draw adds one to both teams' draws ($0B43) and 5 points each. Then each team's score in tens (its hundreds and tens digits, $4B and $49 for team $3C, $4C and $4A for $3D: one point for every 10 scored) goes on its points, its goals for ($0B63/$0B73) and the other's goals against ($0B83/$0B93).
The packed routine league_result unpacks to $C000 and runs.

Sorts the league: $0B23 holds each team's place (low nibble; 0-7 division 2, 8-15 division 1, higher is better) and its place before (high nibble). Builds the list of teams by place at $0920 and sorts each division (sort_division) by points, and level on points by goals for less goals against (league_better), moving a team with fewer points down.
The bubble sort for the eight teams from X.
Compares teams X and Y: points ($0BB3, $0BA3), then goals for less goals against. Carry clear and not equal when Y is ahead.

Plays a match between two computer teams $3C and $3D without showing it, through the packed routine after the JSR (run_packed): sets $3A (0 draw, 1 team $3C won, 2 team $3D won) and the two scores in tens: their hundreds and tens digits ($4B, $49 and $4C, $4A), with the units ($47, $48) zero.

The packed routine simulate_match unpacks to $C000: the two teams' strengths (team_strength) make a score ($C03B): a random number from 0 to 99 is compared with a range set by the difference in strength ($28 more per point of difference for the stronger team, $14 less for the weaker), and its distance from the range picks one of the 44 scores in the table at $C0AF (from 1-0 up to 10-0), given to the stronger team or the weaker; inside the range both teams score the same.
This symbol is the false target of the BIT that skips a LDY #$55 at $5079 (print_char's second entry): it marks no data.
The rest of simulate_match's packed routine: the score table at $C0AF, from 1-0 up to 10-0.
Starts the transfer market: each of the 14 star players (names from $0F45: SHORN to JAMS) gets a random wait of 4-11 weeks ($0BC6), and the three places on offer ($0BC3-$0BC5) are empty.

A week of the transfer market: each star's wait counts down and starts again at 4-7; the empty places on offer take stars whose wait is at 3, from all 14 in a cup, from the first seven while the player's team is in division 2 (bit 3 of $0B23) and from the last seven in division 1.

A screen that waits for fire with a band of colour (colour_band) the stick changes: left and right step $0C0F through the eight colour pairs of band_colours; entered at $5710 with a second band (colour_band_2). RUN/STOP goes back to the main menu.
Steps $0C0F one way for left (bit 2) or the other for right (bit 3) of the stick bits in A, and redraws the band.
Fills 19 rows of 35 cells of the screen at $CC7A with colour pair $0C0F from band_colours.
Fills every other row of 17 at $CCA2 with the opposite pair (band_colours entry $0C0F + 4).
Eight screen colour bytes (high nibble and low nibble the two colours of the multicolour bitmap) for colour_band.

The NEXT FIXTURE screen: the two teams' names ($3C and $3D) with VS between them, and each team's record and squad bars (fixture_week, team_record_text). In a two-player game the second team's bars are the other player's squad (swap_squads, bar_scale, swap_squads). Then colour_screen; fire goes on.
Prints the fixture's week or round by the game type ($0AAC).
The STATISTICS screen after a match: the 16 counters at $0BFB (shots at goal, goals scored, tackles, saves, possession and the rest) for both teams, then bonus points.

Draws a cup or league screen (tile_screen_c8), with a line across for the league types, and lists round A's fixtures: the pairs of teams at $0B23 for a cup, the week's fixtures (fixtures, $7393) otherwise.

Prints each fixture of the round from the last: the pair of teams (from $0B23 in a cup, from week_fixtures otherwise), their names and both scores (result_scores, from $0BDB-$0BF3), always, since the screen is shown after the round is played; then RESULTS.

The league table of the division Brutal Deluxe are in (bit 3 of their place): each team's place, name, won, drawn, lost and points (league_row), with the week; fire goes on, RUN/STOP to the main menu.
Prints one row of the league table.
Where league_table prints its rows and columns: screen addresses and colours.
The league table's row addresses, low bytes; high bytes at $5B3C.
The high bytes.
The league table's colour addresses for each row, low and high ($5B4C).
The high bytes of the league table's colour addresses.
The fixture list's row addresses (low and high at $5B5C).
The high bytes of the fixture list's row addresses.
Prints player name A (the Nth name from $0ED9, BARRY on) at ($1A).
Prints team name A (the Nth from $0E11, BRUTAL DELUXE on) at ($1A).
print_team with the name already counted from team_names.
An entry that prints a player's name (from $0ED9) like print_team_name; nothing calls it.
Prints team X's name and its line of the fixture.
Prints team X's name at the row's place (print_team_name), the entry print_fixture takes for the second team.
Moves ($1C) on past A strings ending in 0: the Nth name of a list.

Prints the text at ($1C) into the bitmap at ($1A) in the mini font (print_char): ASCII from $0F up; 0 ends; 1-8 are commands from text_commands: a new line, a gap, numbers, a team's position and underlining.

The addresses of print_text's commands 1-8 (entry 0 unused): 1 ($5C1D) a new line, ten pixel rows down; 2 n ($5C2F) moves n cells right; 3, 4 and 7 ($5C4F, $5C55, $5C5B) print a number read through the bytes that follow (value_read at $5C6A) in different forms; 5 ($5C83) a team's position in its division (8 less its place within it); 6 ($5C92) a number from the team's ratings; 8 n ($5C3F) n underline characters.
The high bytes of text_commands' addresses.
Command 1 of print_text: a new line, $140 bytes on in the bitmap (one text row, eight pixel rows).
Command 2: moves right by the cells in the next byte.
Moves ($1A) on by A cells of the bitmap (8 bytes each).
Command 8: prints the next byte's number of underline characters.
Command 3: a number (value_read) printed by j_5D58.
Command 4: a number printed by j_5D49.
Command 7: a number printed by j_5CF1.
Takes the next byte of the text at ($1C).
Reads the number a text command names: the address in the next two bytes of the text (or a team's entry), its value in A.
Command 5: the team's position in its division, 8 less its place within it.
Command 6: a number from the team's ratings.
Prints the digit in A.
Prints a value in decimal (gym prices and attributes).
Prints a number of up to three digits.
Splits a value into its decimal digits.
Prints a character with print_char (the formation picture's numbers).

The texts the menu screens print with print_text: the league table's heading and columns, WEEK, RESULTS, NEXT FIXTURE, VS, the STATISTICS screen's lines (SHOTS AT GOAL, GOALS SCORED ... BONUS POINTS) with their commands.
Inside menu_texts: BIT $5DA5 at $33C4 skips a two-byte instruction there; nothing reads this text through the symbol.
The league table's ruled line under the heading, in the mini font's line characters.
One row of the league table: won, drawn and lost ($0B33, $0B43, $0B53) and the points ($0BB3, $0BA3) through print_text's number commands.
DIVISION 1, the league table's title in division 1.
DIVISION 2.
RESULTS, the title of the week's results.
The two scores of a result ($0BDB, $0BEB and $0BE3, $0BF3).
NEXT FIXTURE.
VS between the two teams' names.
The next fixture screen's record of the player's team: won, drawn, lost and points, league place, points for and against, and the headings DEFENCE, MIDFIELD, ATTACK and SUBSTITUTES for its squad.
STATISTICS, the screen's title.
The statistics screen's lines: SHOTS AT GOAL, GOALS SCORED, GOALS SAVED, TIME IN POSSESSION, TIME IN OPPONENTS HALF, SUCCESSFUL TACKLES, SUBSTITUTIONS and BONUS POINTS.
The statistics screen's numbers: eight counters from $0BFB on, two bytes apart, through print_text's command 7.

The gym, before a match: draws the gym screen (tile_screen with the screen at $F400 underneath), the squad's portraits and attribute bars, the bank and the eight attribute buttons; then runs its loop (gym_loop).

The gym's controls: the stick moves the cursor over the 24 buttons (gym_buttons marks which exist), fire presses one: ESC (5) leaves for the match, FIX (6) shows the next fixture, the arrows (13, 14) pick the next or previous player, 1-3 pick a group of players, ALL (10) buys every attribute for the player, and the eight attribute buttons ($10-$17) pick an attribute or, picked again, buy it (gym_buy). In a two-player game each coach uses his own stick.
Moves the gym's cursor to button X with a click (effect $22).

A menu frame: waits for the frame, reads the controls and sorts the sprites. RUN/STOP goes back to the main menu. With the cheat on ($0C10), the + key adds 100 to the bank ($0AB3, decimal) each press.
Lights gym button A (its sprite colour $0838,x).
Dims gym button A.
Shows gym button A pressed.
Places the gym's sprites for the button group A: frames, columns and rows from $66DE, $6696 and $66BA.

When the chosen attribute ($33, 0-7) changes: prints the name of the equipment that trains it (armour_names, through nth_string) in the gym's sprite text, and its price for the chosen group: the attribute's price (attribute_prices, decimal turned to binary) times the group's size (group_size).
Clears the area for the player's name.
The names of the eight pieces of equipment the gym sells, one for each attribute: BITMAP SHADES, BARGE PADS, CHEST GUARD, SPEED BOOTS, POWER ELBOWS, POWER GLOVES, THUNDA THIGHS and BRAIN BOOST.
Buys attribute $33 for each player of the chosen group ($37) in turn (squad_raise, from the group's first place in bar_places), each up to the limit gym_price gives; then shows the bank (bank_show).

Raises attribute A of squad place X by 10 ($0AC3 + 12 x A + X) and pays its price (attribute_prices) from the bank (bank_pay). When the bank cannot pay nothing changes; when the attribute would pass 255 or the limit in $28 (gym_price), the payment is given back with the refusal effect $24.
Takes the price off the bank ($0AB1, $0AB3, decimal), with the till effect.
Adds to the bank.

The main menu, and where RUN/STOP and RESTORE lead: resets the stack and the game (new_game_state), gives team 2 the first computer team's ratings and runs menu 0 (run_menu: 1 PLAYER GAME, 2 PLAYER GAME, DEMO). 1 PLAYER GAME gives menu 2 (KNOCKOUT, LEAGUE, CUP, PRACTICE) and LEAGUE menu 3 (NEW GAME, TEAM GAME, LOAD GAME); 2 PLAYER GAME gives menu 1 (ONE MATCH, BEST OF THREE, BEST OF FIVE). Shows the text at (X, Y) on a plain screen (tile_screen_cc) and waits for fire (wait_fire).

A two-player series of 1, 3 or 5 matches (menu 1): both squads start with 170 ($AA) in every attribute ($0AC3, $0B23) and 1100 in the bank; before each match PLAYER ONE and then PLAYER TWO visit the gym with their own squad (swap_squads between), then the match (two_player_result). At the end the screen names the side that won more matches, or a draw.
Which side starts each match of a two-player series.

A knockout: the bank starts at 1100, and the player's team meets computer teams 1 to 15 in turn, each after the next fixture screen and the gym (team_2_ratings, match_result). A draw is played again, a defeat ends it, and beating team 15 goes back to the main menu.
A cup: the bank starts at 2000, the transfer market starts, and the rounds begin (cup_round).

One round of the cup: the teams not yet knocked out ($0B33 zero) are shuffled into ties ($0B23 pairs). Each tie without the player's team (team 0) is simulated twice, two legs added up (cup_record), and again while the total is level; the player's tie is played over two legs with the ends changed (manager screen, match_result), again while level; the losers are knocked out (cup_loser), the round's results are shown (cup_screen). Knocked out, the player goes back to the main menu; after the fourth round, the final, CONGRATULATIONS! YOU WON THE CUP!
Knocks out the loser of a tie: one more for team $3D's $0B33 when the result $3A is 1, for team $3C's otherwise.
A random team number from 0 to 13.
The last tie of each round of the cup, counting from 0: 7, 3, 1, 0 (8, 4, 2 and 1 ties).

A league (menu 3): a new game (carry clear) starts with 1100 in the bank and the transfer market; LOAD GAME (carry set) carries on from the loaded week. The league is two divisions of eight: places 0-7 are division 2 and 8-15 division 1, the higher the better, and Brutal Deluxe (team 0) start in place 0.
Starts half a season: shuffles the order of the seven weeks of fixtures ($0BD4-$0BDA) and starts at week 1.

A week of the league: the week's eight matches (week_fixtures), the player's with the next fixture screen and the manager screen (league_match), the rest simulated, each recorded (league_result); then the transfer market's week, the table sorted (league_sort), the results and the table shown. Seven weeks make half a season; the second half plays the fixtures again with the ends changed ($0AB0). After the season the top of division 2 (place 7) and the bottom of division 1 (place 8) change places.

The play-off after a season: second in division 2 (place 6) against second from bottom in division 1 (place 9), played again until one wins, who takes the higher place. Then the table and the transfer market. Brutal Deluxe at the top of division 1 (place 15) have won the league (YO! YOU DID IT!); in division 1 after the first season they are promoted (CONGRATULATIONS ON YOUR PROMOTION!) and play a second season; otherwise the game goes back to the main menu.
Plays a league match between teams $3C and $3D: simulated when neither is Brutal Deluxe (team 0), otherwise played after the next fixture screen and the manager screen (match_result).
A random number from 0 to 5, for shuffling the weeks.

Plays a two-player match (play_match) and shows the winner's message; returns the result in A.

The result screen after a one-player match: for a win a message, then A WIN FOR and the winner's name; for a defeat a message, the picture at $7AFC (show_picture_7afc) and A WIN FOR the other team; for a draw a message. Returns the result in A (0 draw, 1 win, 2 defeat).

For each game type, the most coins a match can earn ($0AB5).
For each game type, the fewest coins a team that picked up any is paid for ($0AB6): 3 in a team game, 0 otherwise; a team with none is paid nothing (play_coins).

Plays a match: sets the mode and the coin limits for the game type, resets the scores and the clock, sets up the match (match_setup) and lets the interrupt play it, redrawing the pitch when asked ($8B), until the match state ($45) has bit 7. Then fades out, ends any token or armour and puts back the sprite frames the match changed (sprite_copy). State 5 (a goal) or 7 (an injury) shows its message and kicks off again; state 3 (RUN/STOP) goes back to the main menu, or with the cheat on ($0C10) counts the match as finished; at half time the teams change ends with a message. At the end it adds the goals and saves to the statistics, pays each team its coins (play_coins) at 1, 2 or 4 a coin by the game and round, and sets the result $3A (0 a draw, 1 or 2 the winner).
Resets the clock and plays a half (play_match's second half).

Pays team Y's coins ($4F,y), held between the game type's limits ($0AB6 fewest, $0AB5 most), into its bank, which is decimal: $0AB3,y the hundreds and $0AB1,y the tens and units.
